{{UIHowTo}} __NOTOC__
The addon namespace is a private table shared between Lua files in the same addon. <br>It allows for addons to access data between files without exposing or polluting variables to the global environment.
 addonName, addonTable = ...

==Vararg==
;addonName : <span class="apitype">string</span> - The name of your addon as in the [[TOC_format|TOC]] file and folder name.
;addonTable : <span class="apitype">table</span> - The shared addon table between the Lua files of an addon.

==Example==
This addon defines the "foo" key on the addon table in <code>FileA.lua</code> and accesses it in <code>FileB.lua</code>

'''<span class="apialt">MyAddon.toc</span>'''
 ## Interface: {{API_LatestInterface}}
 ## Version: 1.0.0
 ## Title: Test
 
 FileA.lua
 FileB.lua

'''<span class="apialt">FileA.lua</span>'''
* Note that the underscore "_" here is used as a [https://stackoverflow.com/a/34476033/1297035 throwaway variable] when we don't really care about it.
<syntaxhighlight lang="lua">
local _, ns = ...
ns.foo = "Banana"
</syntaxhighlight>

'''<span class="apialt">FileB.lua</span>'''
<syntaxhighlight lang="lua">
local addonName, ns = ...
print(addonName, ns.foo) -- prints "MyAddon" and "Banana"
</syntaxhighlight>

==Global variable==
You can also simply use a ''unique'' global variable accross your files.

'''<span class="apialt">FileA.lua</span>'''
<syntaxhighlight lang="lua">
MyAddon = {}
MyAddon.apples = 0

function MyAddon:DoSomething(increment)
	self.apples = self.apples + increment
end

MyAddon:DoSomething(2)
</syntaxhighlight>
'''<span class="apialt">FileB.lua</span>'''
<syntaxhighlight lang="lua">
MyAddon:DoSomething(3)
print(MyAddon.apples) -- 5
</syntaxhighlight>
